flawed_step: The proof attempt fails at the inference that a positive s-t flow must use at least two arcs. Looplessness does not prohibit the direct arc s→t, and isolated vertices are explicitly permitted.
counterexample: Take vertices {s,t,u,v}, with u and v isolated, and exactly one arc s→t of capacity 1. Define f(s→t)=1. This is feasible and has value 1. The cut {s} has capacity 1, so no flow can have value greater than 1; hence F=1 and f is maximum. Yet f is positive on exactly one arc, whereas F+1=2.
assessment_summary: The statement is false because a four-vertex network may contain a direct unit-capacity s→t arc while its other two vertices are isolated.
